items.prompt: A VIEWER collaborator sends PUT /api/notes/:id to edit a note that is ARCHIVED. Which response do they get?
items.answer: 409 NOTE_ARCHIVED, as the archive check runs first
distractors: 403 FORBIDDEN, as a viewer row does not carry edit rights
404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND, as archived notes are hidden
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as the body is not accepted
items.explanation: assertCanEditNote tests noteStatus === "ARCHIVED" before canEdit, so even a viewer who could never edit is told to restore the note first.

items.prompt: A signed-in MEMBER who is not a collaborator requests GET /api/notes/<an existing note id>. What comes back?
items.answer: 404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND, the same as for a missing note
distractors: 403 FORBIDDEN, because the note exists but is not shared
200 with the note shown in a read-only view
401 UNAUTHENTICATED, as the user lacks access
items.explanation: findAccessibleById scopes members to notes where they have a collaborator row, so the note is not found and the service throws 404. The member cannot tell "not shared with me" from "does not exist".

items.prompt: An EDITOR collaborator tries to share the note with a teammate through POST /api/notes/:id/share. What happens?
items.answer: 403 FORBIDDEN, as only owners may manage sharing
distractors: 200, as editors may add viewers to a note but not owners
404 USER_NOT_FOUND, before any role is checked
422, as editors may only send a VIEWER grant
items.explanation: canManageSharing is isOwner, which is false for an EDITOR row, so assertCanManageSharing throws 403 before the email is even looked up.

items.prompt: The note owner shares the note with an email address that has no user account yet. Which response does the API return?
items.answer: 404 USER_NOT_FOUND, as there is no user with that email
distractors: 201, and a pending invitation is created for that email
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as the email is not a registered one
200, and a new user is created on the spot with that email
items.explanation: After the sharing check passes, upsertCollaborator looks the email up and throws 404 USER_NOT_FOUND. There is no sign-up route and no invitation model.

items.prompt: A co-owner (a collaborator row with OWNER, not the Note.ownerId user) tries to set the Note.ownerId user to EDITOR. What happens?
items.answer: 422 INVALID_PERMISSION_CHANGE, and the ownerId user keeps OWNER
distractors: It is accepted, as co-owners may change any collaborator
403 FORBIDDEN, as only the Note.ownerId user may manage sharing
409, as a note must keep more than one OWNER row on it
items.explanation: Co-owners pass assertCanManageSharing, but upsertCollaborator refuses any non-OWNER permission for the user whose id is note.ownerId.

items.prompt: A co-owner (OWNER row, not Note.ownerId) grants OWNER to an existing EDITOR. What happens?
items.answer: It is accepted and audited, making the editor a co-owner
distractors: 403, as only the Note.ownerId user may grant OWNER rights
422, as OWNER is not an accepted value in shareNoteSchema
It is accepted, but the new co-owner cannot change status
items.explanation: isOwner is true for any OWNER row, so co-owners pass assertCanManageSharing. shareNoteSchema accepts any NotePermission, and the new OWNER row also gets canArchive. This is finding F6.

items.prompt: A save passes the baseVersionNumber pre-check, but the conditional update then matches zero rows because another save won. What happens?
items.answer: 409 VERSION_CONFLICT, with no conflict audit row written
distractors: 409 VERSION_CONFLICT, and NOTE_CONFLICT_REJECTED is audited
500, as the transaction fails when the update matches nothing
200, as the pre-check already passed, so the save is applied
items.explanation: Only the pre-check path writes NOTE_CONFLICT_REJECTED. In the race path the transaction returns null and the service throws the same 409 without any audit call (finding F3).

items.prompt: A signed-in user POSTs to /api/notes with the body {not json. Which status comes back?
items.answer: 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, as the parse error is not an AppError
distractors: 400, as invalid JSON is the classic bad request status for it
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as parseSchema rejects the body payload
401, as an unreadable body is treated as an unauthenticated call
items.explanation: request.json() throws a SyntaxError before parseSchema runs; apiError maps only AppError instances, so everything else becomes 500 (finding F1).

items.prompt: A signed-in user creates a note whose title is two characters long (the minimum is three). What does the API return?
items.answer: 422 VALIDATION_ERROR with the flattened zod issues
distractors: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with the raw zod error object
500, since a zod error is not mapped by apiError
201, since titles are trimmed but never measured
items.explanation: parseSchema uses safeParse and throws appError(..., 422, "VALIDATION_ERROR", result.error.flatten()), which apiError maps to its own status.

items.prompt: The note owner sends PATCH /api/notes/:id/status with status ARCHIVED for a note that is already ARCHIVED. What happens?
items.answer: 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION, as the note is already archived
distractors: 200, and a second NOTE_STATUS_CHANGED audit row is written
403, as an archived note can be restored by an admin user alone
422, as ARCHIVED is not a valid target status for the route
items.explanation: After assertCanChangeStatus, updateStatus rejects a same-state change with 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION. Two concurrent archives that both read ACTIVE would still both write (finding F5).

items.prompt: The note owner shares an ARCHIVED note with a teammate as VIEWER. What happens?
items.answer: The share is accepted and audited, though the note is archived
distractors: 409 NOTE_ARCHIVED, as the note must be restored before sharing
403, as archiving removes the capabilities of the note owner
422, as only an OWNER grant is allowed on an archived note
items.explanation: Archiving clears canEdit, but canManageSharing stays isOwner, and assertCanManageSharing does not look at the status. The design doc records this as a partial transition guard (check S6).

items.prompt: A user whose session row has expired clicks a raw POST /api/auth/logout. What happens to their cookie?
items.answer: It stays: withAuth returns 401 before the handler clears it
distractors: It is cleared, as logout works even for a stale session
It is cleared, and the expired session row is deleted as well
It stays, but the expired session row is deleted by the call
items.explanation: withAuth resolves no session and returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED without calling the handler, so clearSessionCookie never runs (finding F9).

items.front: What does getNoteAccessLevel return for an EDITOR on an ACTIVE note, and for any collaborator on an ARCHIVED note?
items.back: EDITOR on ACTIVE: canEdit true, canManageSharing false, canArchive false. On ARCHIVED, canEdit is false for everyone (admins too), while canManageSharing and canArchive keep their values. A member with no collaborator row gets 404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND.

items.front: Why does a non-collaborator get 404 while a viewer who tries to share gets 403?
items.back: Reads are scoped by buildAccessibleNoteWhere, so a member who is not a collaborator never sees the note and gets 404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND; they cannot tell "not shared" from "missing". A collaborator can see it, so lacking a capability is reported as 403.

items.front: How is a note save protected against concurrent edits?
items.back: A pre-check compares currentVersionNumber with baseVersionNumber (409 VERSION_CONFLICT plus a NOTE_CONFLICT_REJECTED audit). Inside the transaction a conditional updateMany on the expected version, backed by @@unique([noteId, versionNumber]), catches the race; losing it also returns 409, but without an audit row.

items.front: Summarize the session lifecycle in Collab Notes.
items.back: 32 random bytes as a hex token; only sha256(token:SESSION_SECRET) is stored; fixed 14-day expiry (lastSeenAt is updated but never extends it); every API request looks the session up and reads the user role; expired rows are never cleaned up, and logout needs a live session.
